plan.title: SRC-AWD-012 — Award non-lowest bid and reject proposal

steps.note: the API built this case's state
Use an RFQ stage rather than the default auction stage.
Configure the RFQ stage before selecting its template and line items.
Apply the pricing template required for the RFQ sheet.
Create one line with the requested quantity of 10 units.
Complete the RFQ pricing sheet so the event can be published.
Commit a bidding schedule before publishing.
Invite two vendors so the event can receive the two competing bids.
Submit the higher-priced bid that represents Vendor A’s 10-unit bid.
Confirm the first vendor’s bid was accepted.
Submit the second, lower bid for another invited vendor so Vendor A is not the lowest bidder.
Confirm the second bid was accepted.
Close bidding so awarding is available.
Open the buyer comparison grid for the two submitted bids.
Verify both vendor columns are present with real names.
Verify Vendor A’s bid rate is 100.
Verify the lower-priced bid ranks ahead of Vendor A.
Open the awarding screen.
Allocate the full 10-unit line to the portal bidder, Vendor A, rather than the lower bid.
Verify the line is fully selected and only one of two vendors is awarded.
Create the award proposal from the allocation.
Verify the proposal page opened.

args.goal: fill the required proposal fields and submit the proposal; stop on the submitted proposal screen showing that it is awaiting approval

steps.note: Complete proposal fields that have no dedicated catalog step and submit the proposal.
Confirm the submitted proposal is awaiting approval.

args.need: sign in as the approver, open the submitted proposal, reject it with a remark, verify no purchase order is created, return to the buyer, and verify awarding can be started again from Master QCS

steps.note: The approver’s separate login and rejection workflow are not available to the catalog.
After the tester completes the rejection and returns to the buyer, reopen Master QCS to check the recovery path.
Attempt to restart awarding after the rejected proposal.
Assert that a fresh awarding flow is available with no current allocation.
